survey: An inflatable beach ball resting on rippled sand, seen from slightly above and in front. It has six gore panels that alternate white with colour: red, white, blue, white, green, white. All six meet at a purple circular cap at the upper pole, which faces the camera a little toward the front. The seams run from the cap down and around the ball and curve toward a lower pole hidden under the ball. The sphere is round and sits on the sand with a contact shadow, so it is supported and does not float. The panel count, the alternating order and the single pole cap match a real beach ball. There are no invented parts.

errors.where: Front of the ball, the white panel between the red and blue panels, compared with the blue panel to its right
errors.what: The panels are not equal widths. On a real beach ball every gore spans the same 60° slice. The front white panel faces the camera most directly, so it should look widest, but it is only about half as wide at the equator as the blue panel beside it, which turns away from the viewer. The seams do not divide the sphere evenly, so the panel layout could not be sewn from six identical gores.

fix: Beach ball made of six equal-width gore panels alternating white, red, white, blue, white, green, all meeting evenly at the purple top cap; panel widths follow correct spherical perspective so the front-facing panel appears widest and side panels narrow evenly toward the silhouette.
